questions.question: During the Delhi Sultanate period, which one of the following taxes was levied on treasure looted in war?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khums**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Khums** was a tax levied during the **Delhi Sultanate** period on the treasure or booty looted in wars.
 
• The term **Khums** literally means "one-fifth" in Arabic, and it refers to the Islamic principle of taxing one-fifth (20%) of the war booty.
 
• This tax was collected by the state and was utilized for administrative purposes, public welfare, and religious activities.
 
• The remaining four-fifths of the booty were distributed among the soldiers who participated in the battle, as per Islamic law.
 
• The practice of levying **Khums** was in line with the Islamic traditions followed by the rulers of the Delhi Sultanate, such as the Slave Dynasty, Khilji Dynasty, and Tughlaq Dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kharaj:**

 
 
• Kharaj was a **land tax** imposed on agricultural produce during the Delhi Sultanate period.
 
• It was usually levied on non-Muslim cultivators and was a significant source of revenue for the state.
 
• The tax rate varied but was typically fixed at one-third of the total agricultural produce.
 
 
 
• **Jizyah:**
 
 
• Jizyah was a tax levied on **non-Muslims** (referred to as Dhimmis) for protection and exemption from military service.
 
• This tax was an important financial contribution made by non-Muslim subjects to the Islamic state.
 
• Jizyah was abolished by Akbar but reinstated by Aurangzeb during the Mughal period.
 
 
 
• **Zakat:**
 
 
• Zakat is a **form of almsgiving** and one of the Five Pillars of Islam.
 
• It was a mandatory charitable contribution levied on Muslims, typically amounting to 2.5% of one’s wealth.
 
• Zakat was used for social welfare and assistance to the poor and needy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Islamic Taxation System:**

 
 
• The taxation system during the Delhi Sultanate was heavily influenced by Islamic principles.
 
• Taxes like Khums, Zakat, and Jizyah were based on Islamic jurisprudence and were used to maintain the state's administration and support religious institutions.
 
• These taxes were systematically collected and documented by state-appointed officials.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Use of Taxes:**
 
 
• The revenue collected through Khums and other taxes was used for state welfare, construction of mosques, fortifications, and public works.
 
• It also funded the military campaigns and administrative machinery of the Sultanate.

questions.question: As of 31st July 2025, which of the following country is NOT the member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)** is a regional grouping established in **1967** that promotes economic, political, and security cooperation among its **10 member countries** located primarily in Southeast Asia.
 
• The **founding members** of ASEAN include **Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand**, which signed the Bangkok Declaration in **August 1967**.
 
• Other members include **Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, and Cambodia**, totalling 5 members. These countries work together to enhance regional cooperation and integration.
 
• **Pakistan** is not a member of ASEAN. It is located in South Asia and is a member of other organisations like **SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation)**, but it does not participate in the ASEAN framework.
 
• Countries like **Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines**, mentioned in the question, are prominent members of ASEAN and actively contribute to its initiatives. *Hence, Pakistan is not part of ASEAN.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ASEAN:**

 
 
• **Established:** **8 August 1967**, Bangkok, Thailand.
 
• **Objective:** To accelerate economic growth, social progress, and cultural development in the region.
 
• **Headquarters:** Jakarta, Indonesia.
 
• **ASEAN Charter:** Signed in **November 2007** and entered into force in **December 2008**. It serves as the legal and institutional framework for ASEAN.
 
 
 
• **​Recent** **Summits:**
 
 
• **​47th ASEAN Summit**:
 
 
• Held on 26–28 October 2025 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre (KLCC), Malaysia.
 
• On 26 October 2025, **Timor-Leste** formally signed the accession instrument to become ASEAN's 11th Member State.
 
• A landmark agreement (**Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord**) between **Thailand and Cambodia** was signed during the 47th Summit to resolve long-standing border conflicts.
 
 
 
• **ASEAN-India Summit**: At the **22nd ASEAN-India Summit**, Prime Minister Narendra Modi declared 2026 as the "ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation".
 
• **Current Chairmanship**: The **Philippines** holds the rotating ASEAN Chairmanship for **2026**.
 
 
 
• **ASEAN's Economic Role:**
 
 
• ASEAN is one of the most dynamic economic regions in the world, with a combined GDP exceeding **$3 trillion**.
 
• It has established various free trade agreements (FTAs) with countries like **China, Japan, South Korea, India, Australia, and New Zealand**.
 
• The **Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP)**, signed in **2020**, further strengthens ASEAN's global economic integration.
 
 
 
• **Important Members of ASEAN:**
 
 
• **Indonesia:** The largest economy in ASEAN and a founding member.
 
• **Malaysia:** Known for its advanced infrastructure and active participation in ASEAN initiatives.
 
• **Philippines:** A founding member with a focus on regional security and economic development.
 
• **Brunei:** A small but wealthy member contributing to ASEAN's energy sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ASEAN's Dialogue Partners:** ASEAN collaborates with **its dialogue partners,** including the **USA, China, India, Japan, South Korea, and Russia,** to discuss geopolitical and economic issues.
 
• **ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF):** Established in **1994**, the ARF promotes regional security and confidence-building measures.
 
• **ASEAN Economic Community (AEC):** Launched in **2015**, the AEC aims to create a single market and production base among ASEAN member states.
 
• **ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA):** AFTA was established in **1992** to promote intra-regional trade by reducing tariff barriers.

questions.question: What name was given to Bal Gangadhar Tilak by the British rulers?

options.text: The Father of the Indian Unrest

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Father of the Indian Unrest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** was given the title "**The Father of the Indian Unrest**" by the British colonial rulers due to his revolutionary ideas and activities in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• This title was coined by the British writer and historian **Valentine Chirol** in his book titled "Indian Unrest" published in the early 20th century.
 
• Tilak’s strong opposition to British rule and his call for **Swaraj (self-rule)** resonated strongly among Indians, making him a prominent leader in the freedom movement.
 
• He played a crucial role in the **extremist faction** of the Indian National Congress, advocating for direct confrontation with colonial authorities rather than moderate dialogue.
 
• His famous statement, "**Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it**," became a rallying cry for Indian independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Bal Gangadhar Tilak:**

 
 
• He was born on **23 July 1856** in Ratnagiri, Maharashtra.
 
• Tilak was one of the **earliest leaders of the Indian independence movement** and is often referred to as one of the "Lal-Bal-Pal" trio, along with Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal.
 
• He founded two nationalist newspapers, **Kesari (in Marathi)** and **The Mahratta (in English)**, which were instrumental in spreading anti-British sentiments.
 
• He was also a scholar of Indian culture and wrote extensively on the **Bhagavad Gita** and other Indian scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Other Titles and Contributions:**
 
 
• Despite the British calling him "The Father of the Indian Unrest," Tilak was also referred to as **"Lokmanya,"** meaning "accepted by the people as their leader."
 
• He introduced the **Ganesh Chaturthi** festival as a public event to unite people and instill a sense of nationalism.
 
• He was a key figure in the **Home Rule Movement** in 1916, which aimed to attain self-governance within the British Empire.
 
 
 
• **Context of the Title:**
 
 
• The title "The Father of the Indian Unrest" by **Valentine Chirol** reflected British fears of Tilak's ability to mobilize people against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Titles of other Leaders**:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Valentine Chirol's Role:**

 
 
• Chirol was a British journalist and historian who criticized the Indian independence movement in his writings.
 
• His book "Indian Unrest" was a critique of Indian nationalists, particularly Tilak and his methods.

questions.question: Who was the first recipient of the Best Actor at the National Film Awards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttam Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uttam Kumar** was the first recipient of the **National Film Award for Best Actor**, which was introduced in **1968**.
 
• He received the award for his exceptional performance in the films **"Chiriyakhana"** (directed by Satyajit Ray) and **"Antony Firingee"**.
 
• The National Film Awards are the most prestigious awards for films in India, organized by the **Government of India** to honor excellence in cinema.
 
• **Uttam Kumar** was widely regarded as the icon **of Bengali cinema and had a profound influence on Indian cinema.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Film Awards:**

 
 
• The National Film Awards were established in **1954** and are presented annually by the **Directorate of Film Festivals**, which is part of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
 
• The awards aim to encourage the production of films of high artistic and technical standards and recognize achievements across various categories, including acting, direction, music, and cinematography.
 
• The awards are divided into two main categories: **Feature Films** and **Non-Feature Films**, with additional awards for Best Writing on Cinema.
 
 
 
• **Uttam Kumar's Legacy:**
 
 
• **Uttam Kumar** was born on **3 September 1926** in Kolkata and became one of the most celebrated actors in Bengali cinema.
 
• He worked in over **200 films**, showcasing his talent in both commercial and arthouse cinema.
 
• His collaborations with directors like **Satyajit Ray** and his co-acting with actresses like **Suchitra Sen** are iconic in Indian film history.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the **Dadasaheb Phalke Award**, India's highest honor in cinema.
 
 
 
• **Other Nominees for the First Best Actor Award:**
 
 
• **Prithviraj Kapoor:** A legendary actor known for his contribution to Indian theatre and cinema, but he did not win the first National Film Award for Best Actor.
 
• **Ashok Kumar:** A pioneering figure in Indian cinema, often referred to as the "Dadamoni," he was recognized for his acting skills but was not the first recipient of this award.
 
• **Dev Anand:** Known as the "Evergreen Star" of Bollywood, he was famous for his charismatic performances, but he did not win the first National Film Award for Best Actor.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: "UDISE+" which was in news in February 2025, is related to which of the following sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **UDISE+** stands for **Unified District Information System for Education Plus**.
 
• This system was introduced by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, to strengthen and improve the collection of data related to the **school education system** in India.
 
• **UDISE+** replaces the earlier version, UDISE, and aims to provide accurate and comprehensive data related to **schools, teachers, and students** in both government and private schools.
 
• It facilitates better planning, decision-making, and implementation of policies by providing a transparent and reliable database of the education sector.
 
• The system covers vital aspects such as **student enrollment, infrastructure availability, teacher qualifications, and dropout rates** across schools in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of UDISE+:**

 
 
• UDISE+ ensures **real-time data collection** and reduces manual errors through digitization.
 
• It provides a platform for tracking and monitoring the progress of various government schemes such as **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan** and **Mid-Day Meal Scheme**.
 
• Data collected through UDISE+ is used to generate reports and indices, such as the **Performance Grading Index (PGI)** for states and Union Territories.
 
• The system is designed to ensure **equity, quality, and access** in education.
 
 
 
• **Importance of School Education Data:**
 
 
• Reliable data is crucial for identifying gaps in infrastructure, teacher deployment, and student performance.
 
• It enables the government to allocate resources effectively and prioritize areas that need immediate attention.
 
• Quality data helps in achieving **Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4)**, which focuses on ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Similar systems like UDISE+ are implemented in other countries to monitor education-related progress. For example, UNESCO's **Education Management Information System (EMIS)** aims to collect and analyze data on education globally.
 
• Such systems contribute to international cooperation and knowledge sharing for improving education standards worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UDISE+ Implementation:**

 
 
• The system is applicable across **schools providing elementary, secondary, and higher secondary education** in India.
 
• UDISE+ is managed and monitored by the Department of School Education and Literacy under the Ministry of Education.
 
• Annual surveys conducted through UDISE+ help track the progress of various programs and schemes in the education sector.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges:**
 
 
• Ensuring data accuracy and completeness remains a challenge, especially in remote and rural areas.
 
• Lack of digital infrastructure in some schools hinders the seamless implementation of UDISE+.
 
• Capacity-building initiatives for school administrators and education officials are essential for the effective use of UDISE+.

questions.question: In Union Budget 2025-26, Jal Jeevan Mission has been extended until _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2030**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission** was launched by the **Government of India** on **15th August 2019** to provide **safe and adequate drinking water** through individual household tap connections by 2024 to all rural households.
 
• The mission aims at ensuring **functional tap water connections** to every household in **India's rural areas**.
 
• In the **Union Budget 2025-26**, the Jal Jeevan Mission has been extended until **2030**, marking a significant step toward achieving universal access to clean drinking water.
 
• The extension reflects the government's commitment to addressing issues related to **water scarcity, hygiene, and public health**.
 
• By extending the mission to **2030**, India aligns itself with the **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6**, which focuses on clean water and sanitation for all.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of Jal Jeevan Mission:**

 
 
• The mission seeks to provide **55 liters of water per person per day** to every rural household through **functional household tap connections**.
 
• It emphasizes **community participation** and encourages villages to prepare **water security plans**.
 
• Strengthening the capacity of local bodies, including **Panchayati Raj Institutions**, is a key component of the program.
 
• It also focuses on **source sustainability** measures, such as rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6):**
 
 
• SDG 6 is part of the **United Nations' 2030 Agenda**, aiming to ensure the availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all.
 
• It emphasizes improving water quality, implementing integrated water resource management, and protecting water-related ecosystems.
 
• The Jal Jeevan Mission contributes significantly to India's progress in achieving this global goal.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Addressed by Jal Jeevan Mission:**
 
 
• India faces challenges such as **water scarcity, contamination of water sources**, and poor infrastructure in rural areas.
 
• The mission aims to address these challenges through **technological interventions**, robust infrastructure development, and community involvement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Budget Allocation:**

 
 
• The Union Budget has allocated significant funds to the Jal Jeevan Mission, reflecting its importance in the national development agenda.
 
• In the **Union Budget 2023-24**, approximately **₹60,000 crore** was allocated to the program.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• The mission leverages **smart meters, remote monitoring systems**, and advanced water treatment technologies.
 
• It also promotes the use of **solar-powered water supply systems** in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Community Empowerment:**
 
 
• The program encourages the formation of **Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs)** to ensure efficient management and maintenance.
 
• Training programs are conducted to enhance **local capacity** for water resource management.

questions.question: Which of the following sports is played on water?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Surfing**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Surfing** is a sport performed on water where an individual rides on ocean waves using a surfboard. The participant glides on the wave's face towards the shore. • This sport requires large water bodies, typically oceans, seas, or artificial wave pools, where there are consistent and surfable waves. • Surfing originated in the **Pacific Islands**, with Hawaii being one of the most notable regions where it developed as both a sport and cultural practice. • The equipment primarily includes a **surfboard**, which comes in various sizes and designs depending on the surfer's skill level and wave conditions. • Surfing has become a popular recreational activity worldwide and is also a competitive sport, with events like the **World Surf League (WSL)** and its inclusion in the **Olympics**.

questions.question: The term Decathlon and Heptathlon are related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Athletics events**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decathlon** and **Heptathlon** are multi-event competitions in **track and field athletics**. These events include a mix of running, jumping, and throwing disciplines.
 
• The **Decathlon** is a ten-event competition, typically conducted over two days, and is primarily for men. It includes events such as 100m sprint, long jump, shot put, high jump, 400m race, 110m hurdles, discus throw, pole vault, javelin throw, and 1500m race.
 
• The **Heptathlon** is a seven-event competition, primarily for women. It includes 100m hurdles, high jump, shot put, 200m sprint, long jump, javelin throw, and 800m race.
 
• Both Decathlon and Heptathlon are designed to test an athlete's **versatility**, endurance, speed, strength, and technique across a diverse range of events.
 
• These events are typically part of international athletics championships, such as the **Olympic Games**, **World Athletics Championships**, and **Commonwealth Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Decathlon and Heptathlon:**

 
 
• The modern Decathlon was first introduced in the **1912 Stockholm Olympics**. It was inspired by the ancient Greek pentathlon, which featured five events.
 
• The Heptathlon for women was introduced later, replacing the Pentathlon in major competitions, and became an Olympic event in the **1984 Los Angeles Games**.
 
 
 
• **Scoring System:**
 
 
• Both Decathlon and Heptathlon use a **points-based system** to determine the winner. Points are awarded based on the performance in each event, using pre-determined tables created by the **World Athletics** governing body.
 
• The athlete with the highest total points at the end of all events is declared the winner.
 
 
 
• **Famous Athletes:**
 
 
• Notable Decathletes include **Daley Thompson** (UK), **Ashton Eaton** (USA), and **Roman Šebrle** (Czech Republic).
 
• Prominent Heptathletes include **Jackie Joyner-Kersee** (USA), **Jessica Ennis-Hill** (UK), and **Nafissatou Thiam** (Belgium).
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Badminton match types:** Badminton matches are categorized based on the format, such as singles or doubles, and not related to Decathlon or Heptathlon.
 
• **Swimming styles:** Swimming competitions include styles like freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly, which are distinct from athletics events.
 
• **Golf area types:** Golf uses terms like fairway, rough, bunker, and green to describe the playing field, unrelated to Decathlon or Heptathlon.

questions.question: The 8th India Water Week 2024 was held during 17-20 September 2024, in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **8th India Water Week (IWW) 2024** was organized in **New Delhi**, the national capital of India. The event was held from **17th to 20th September 2024**.
 
• The theme for the 8th India Water Week 2024 was **“Water Security for Sustainable Development”**, focusing on the judicious use of water resources for sustainable economic development and environmental management.
 
• The event was organized by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, Government of India, in association with several national and international partners.
 
• India Water Week serves as a platform for **policymakers, experts, and stakeholders** from across the globe to discuss and collaborate on water management strategies and solutions.
 
• The event featured **exhibitions, workshops, and panel discussions** showcasing advancements in water conservation techniques, irrigation technologies, and water resource management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India Water Week:**

 
 
• India Water Week is a flagship event organized by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** to address critical water-related issues and explore solutions for sustainable water management.
 
• It was first organized in **2012**, and since then, it has been held biennially, attracting participation from **national and international experts**, government officials, and industry leaders.
 
• The event focuses on themes such as **water conservation, irrigation, flood management, and wastewater treatment**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Jal Shakti:**

• It is responsible for the **management of water resources**, including drinking water supply, water conservation, and river development projects.
 
• Key initiatives include the **Namami Gange Programme** and the **Jal Jeevan Mission**.
 
 
 
• **Water Security in India:**
 
 
• India is home to **17% of the world's population** but has only **4% of the world's freshwater resources**, making water security a critical concern.
 
• Challenges include **overexploitation of groundwater**, **water pollution**, and **climate change**-induced variations in water availability.
 
• Programs like the **Atal Bhujal Yojana** and the **National Water Mission** aim to address these issues.

• **History of Volleyball:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: As of June 2025, how many Ramsar site are there in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**91**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ramsar Sites** are wetlands of international importance designated under the **Ramsar Convention**, an international treaty signed in **1971** in Ramsar, Iran. These sites are essential for biodiversity conservation and sustainable development.
 
• As of **June 2025**, **India has 91 Ramsar sites**, covering a total area of about **20,758.19 square kilometers**. These sites play a critical role in maintaining ecological balance.
 
• India is one of the contracting parties to the Ramsar Convention since **1982** and has been proactive in identifying and designating wetlands of ecological significance.
 
• The most recent additions to the list include wetlands like **Sakhya Sagar** in Madhya Pradesh and **Pala Wetland** in Mizoram, recognized for their biodiversity and ecological significance.
 
• India has the largest number of Ramsar sites in South Asia, demonstrating its commitment to wetland conservation and sustainable management practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of Ramsar Sites:**

 
 
• Wetlands provide critical ecosystem services such as **flood control, groundwater replenishment, and climate regulation**.
 
• They serve as habitats for a wide variety of **flora and fauna, including migratory birds**, amphibians, and aquatic species.
 
• Many Ramsar sites in India are culturally significant and are linked to the livelihoods of local communities.
 
 
 
• **Notable Ramsar Sites in India:**
 
 
• **Sundarbans Wetland** in West Bengal: It is the largest tidal halophytic mangrove forest in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• **Chilika Lake** in Odisha: Asia's largest brackish water lagoon, known for its rich biodiversity and as a significant bird sanctuary.
 
• **Loktak Lake** in Manipur: Famous for its floating phumdis (heterogeneous masses of vegetation) and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Wetland Conservation:**
 
 
• Wetlands act as **natural water purifiers** by filtering pollutants from water.
 
• They are significant for **carbon sequestration**, helping mitigate climate change.
 
• Wetlands support sustainable livelihoods by providing resources like fish, fodder, and water for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Ramsar Convention:**
 
 
• The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands is an international treaty adopted in **1971** to conserve and sustainably use wetlands.
 
• It emphasizes the "wise use" of wetlands, which involves maintaining their ecological character through sustainable practices.
 
• India is one of the **173 contracting parties** to the convention as of 2025.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Criteria for Ramsar Site Designation:**

 
 
• The site should support vulnerable, endangered, or critically endangered species.
 
• It should be a habitat for flora and fauna during critical stages of their life cycle.
 
• The site must play a significant role in maintaining the biological diversity of the region.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Wetland Conservation:**
 
 
• Threats like **urbanization, pollution, and encroachment** have led to the degradation of wetlands.
 
• Climate change impacts, such as altered rainfall patterns and rising temperatures, threaten wetland ecosystems.
 
• Efforts like community participation and government initiatives are crucial for wetland restoration and management.

questions.question: ’Manimahesh fair’ is held in which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Manimahesh Fair** is an annual pilgrimage held in the state of **Himachal Pradesh**, India.
 
• It is organized at the **Manimahesh Lake**, located near the **Manimahesh Kailash Peak** in the **Bharmour region** of the **Chamba district**.
 
• According to tradition, the fair is held every year during the month of **Bhadrapada** (August-September) as per the **Hindu calendar**.
 
• The Manimahesh Lake is considered to be **holy**, and devotees from across India undertake this pilgrimage to seek blessings from **Lord Shiva**, who is believed to reside in the Manimahesh Kailash Peak.
 
• The fair is a significant religious and cultural event and attracts thousands of pilgrims, especially during the **Janmashtami** and **Radhashtami** festivals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Manimahesh Lake:**

 
 
• The lake is situated at an altitude of approximately **4,080 meters (13,390 feet)** above sea level in the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas.
 
• The name “Manimahesh” translates to the **"jewel of Lord Shiva"**, as the deity is believed to adorn the peak with his divine presence.
 
 
 
• **Manimahesh Kailash Peak:**
 
 
• The **Manimahesh Kailash Peak** is revered as the abode of **Lord Shiva**.
 
• This peak remains unclimbed due to its religious significance, as it is considered sacred by the devotees.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Pilgrimage:**
 
 
• The pilgrimage to Manimahesh Lake is considered equivalent to the **Kailash Mansarovar Yatra** in Tibet.
 
• Pilgrims believe that a dip in the holy lake purifies the soul and washes away sins.
 
 
 
• **Access and Routes:**
 
 
• The **trek** to the lake begins at the **Hadsar village**, which is accessible via Bharmour in the Chamba district.
 
• The route involves a strenuous trek through the scenic and rugged landscapes of the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Other Fairs in Himachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh is renowned for its fairs and festivals, including the **Kullu Dussehra**, **Lavi Fair**, and **Minjar Fair**.
 
• These events reflect the cultural richness and traditional heritage of the state.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Religious Beliefs:** The Manimahesh pilgrimage is deeply rooted in Hindu religious beliefs. It is said that Lord Shiva created the Manimahesh Lake after marrying Goddess Parvati.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** The growing number of pilgrims has raised concerns about **environmental degradation** in the region. Efforts are being made to promote eco-friendly tourism.
 
• **Accessibility:** The pilgrimage is undertaken during specific months due to the extreme weather conditions in the region. The area remains **inaccessible in winter** due to heavy snowfall.

questions.question: The first temple-building activity in India began during the rule of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gupta Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gupta Dynasty** (circa 3rd to 6th century CE) is credited with initiating the first significant temple-building activity in India. Temples built during this period were primarily dedicated to **Hindu deities**, such as Vishnu, Shiva, and Shakti.
 
• The early Gupta temples were typically made of **brick and stone**, showcasing the transition from wood-based structures to more durable materials. This marked the beginning of India's rich temple architecture tradition.
 
• Examples of Gupta temple architecture include the **Dashavatara Temple** in Deogarh and the **Durga Temple** in Aihole. These temples featured simple designs, flat roofs, and intricate carvings that later evolved into more complex structures.
 
• The Gupta Dynasty is often referred to as the **"Golden Age of India"** due to its advancements in art, architecture, literature, and science. Temple-building was an integral part of this cultural resurgence.
 
• The temples built during the Gupta period laid the foundation for the development of **Nagara, Dravidian, and Vesara styles** of temple architecture, which flourished in later centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Gupta Empire ruled over large parts of India between the **3rd and 6th centuries CE**.
 
• It is known for its significant contributions to **Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism**, and its promotion of Sanskrit literature.
 
• Key rulers included **Chandragupta I, Samudragupta**, and **Chandragupta II**, who patronized arts, culture, and temple-building projects.
 
 
 
• **Temple Architecture during Gupta Era:**
 
 
• The temples were small and modest in size but introduced key architectural features like **garbhagriha (sanctum sanctorum)** and **shikhara (spire).**
 
• They primarily used **stone and terracotta** for construction, replacing earlier wooden structures.
 
• The Dashavatara Temple in Deogarh is one of the earliest examples of a **Nagara-style temple** with a square sanctum and intricate carvings.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Ahom Kingdom:**
 
 
• The Ahom Kingdom (1228–1826 CE) was located in present-day Assam and is known for its unique architecture, such as the **Rang Ghar**, but it is not associated with the origins of temple-building in India.
 
 
 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:**
 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646 CE) in South India is famous for its **Dravidian-style temples**, such as the **Virupaksha Temple**, but it came much later than the Gupta period.
 
 
 
• **Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty (8th–11th century CE) significantly contributed to temple architecture, especially in **North India**, but their temple-building activities were inspired by earlier Gupta structures.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Gupta Temples:**
 
 
• The architectural principles established during the Gupta period influenced temple-building activities across India for centuries.
 
• The cultural and religious importance of temples grew during and after the Gupta era, making them centers of devotion, art, and learning.

questions.question: ’Jaago’ dance is related to which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **‘Jaago’ dance** is a traditional folk dance associated with the state of **Punjab**.
 
• ‘Jaago’ literally means "wake up" and is performed during **wedding celebrations** to awaken the village or community to join the festivities.
 
• During this dance, women carry **decorated brass vessels** (often illuminated with oil lamps or candles) on their heads, which adds a spiritual and celebratory element to the performance.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional **Punjabi folk songs** that are sung collectively, often humorously teasing the bride, groom, or their families.
 
• ‘**Jaago**’ reflects the rich cultural heritage of Punjab and is deeply rooted in the traditions and customs of Punjabi weddings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Punjab’s Cultural Significance:**

 
 
• Punjab is known for its vibrant culture, which includes traditional dances like **Bhangra**, **Giddha**, and **Jaago**.
 
• The state has a rich tradition of folk music and dance, which are often performed during festivals, harvests, and other significant occasions.
 
• ‘Jaago’ is particularly significant as it blends **community participation** with a sense of celebration and joy.
 
 
 
• **Other Traditional Dances of Punjab:**
 
 
• **Bhangra:** A high-energy dance performed mostly by men during harvest festivals such as **Baisakhi**.
 
• **Giddha:** A lively women’s dance that involves clapping and singing boliyan (folk couplets).
 
• **Sammi:** A less well-known dance performed by women in rural areas of Punjab, often characterized by slow, graceful movements.
 
 
 
• **Significance of ‘Jaago’:**
 
 
• ‘Jaago’ is symbolic of **community unity and celebration** during weddings, where everyone is invited to join the revelry.
 
• The lit candles or lamps in the brass vessels signify **light and hope** for the new couple's journey ahead.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Elements:**
 
 
• The decorative vessels used in ‘Jaago’ are called **“chajj”** and are adorned with flowers, mirrors, and colorful threads.
 
• The folk songs sung during ‘Jaago’ are often humorous, adding a playful element to the occasion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other States’ Folk Dances:**

 
 
• **Jharkhand:** Known for tribal dances such as **Chhau** and **Paika**, which are distinct from Punjab’s ‘Jaago’ dance.
 
• **Odisha:** Famous for **Odissi dance** and folk dances like **Dalkhai** and **Chhau**. These are classical and tribal in nature.
 
• **Maharashtra:** Popular for **Lavani** and **Koli** dances, showcasing the cultural essence of the state’s fisherfolk and rural communities.

questions.question:
Which of the following organ can be donated while the donor is alive?

I. Part of a liver

II. Kidney
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Living organ donation** allows healthy individuals to donate certain organs or tissues while they are alive to save or enhance the lives of others. This is regulated under strict medical guidelines and ethical considerations.
 
• Part of a liver can be donated by a living donor. The liver has a unique ability to regenerate, making it possible for a portion of the liver to be transplanted while the donor’s liver regrows to its normal size. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• A kidney can be donated by a living donor. Humans typically have two kidneys, and one kidney is sufficient for a donor to live a healthy life while the donated kidney can save the life of the recipient. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• Living organ donation is strictly regulated to ensure the safety of both the donor and the recipient. It requires comprehensive medical evaluations and legal consent processes.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both I and II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Organ Donation:**

 
 
• Organ donation refers to the process of donating organs or tissues from a donor to a recipient. It can be done either after death (cadaveric donation) or by living donors.
 
• Living donors can donate organs like kidneys, part of the liver, or tissues such as bone marrow, provided they meet strict medical criteria.
 
• Organ donations save lives, especially in cases of chronic organ failure such as kidney or liver failure.
 
 
 
• **Liver Donation:**
 
 
• The liver is the only organ in the human body capable of regenerating itself. This allows living donors to donate a portion of their liver, which regrows to its normal size in both the donor and the recipient.
 
• Liver donation typically involves removing either the right or left lobe of the liver, depending on the size and needs of the recipient.
 
• Regeneration usually takes place within a few months of donation.
 
 
 
• **Kidney Donation:**
 
 
• Kidneys are vital for filtering waste and maintaining fluid balance in the body. Living individuals with healthy kidney function can donate one kidney.
 
• A kidney transplant is often the best treatment for end-stage renal disease (ESRD) or chronic kidney failure.
 
• Donors undergo extensive medical evaluations to ensure their remaining kidney can sustain normal kidney function.
 
 
 
• **Legal and Ethical Guidelines:**
 
 
• Organ donation is regulated under laws such as the **Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994,** in India, which ensures ethical practices and prohibits organ trafficking.
 
• Donors must give informed consent, and medical professionals must ensure donors are not coerced or exploited.
 
• Both donor and recipient undergo psychological and medical evaluations to ensure a safe and ethical transplant process.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for Living Donation:**

 
 
• Donors must be in good physical and mental health, typically between the ages of **18 and 60 years**.
 
• They must undergo rigorous medical tests, including blood tests, imaging scans, and psychological assessments.
 
• Living donors are often family members or close relatives of the recipient to reduce the risk of organ rejection.
 
 
 
• **Statistics:**
 
 
• Globally, living organ donation accounts for a significant portion of transplants. For example, in **India**, about **90% of kidney transplants** come from living donors.
 
• Countries like the **United States** and **South Korea** also see high rates of living donation, particularly for kidney and liver transplants.
 
 
 
• **Awareness Campaigns:**
 
 
• Initiatives like **National Organ Donation Day** (celebrated annually on **27th November** in India) aim to educate the public about the life-saving benefits of organ donation.

questions.question: The most important achievement of Shishunaga was ____.

options.text: defeating Avanti (Malwa) and annexing it to Magadh

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**defeating Avanti (Malwa) and annexing it to Magadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Shishunaga**, the founder of the Shishunaga dynasty, ruled Magadh in ancient India and contributed significantly to its expansion.
 
• One of his most notable achievements was **defeating Avanti (Malwa)**, a major kingdom that posed a significant threat to Magadh's dominance.
 
• After defeating Avanti, Shishunaga successfully **annexed the kingdom to Magadh**, thereby strengthening his empire and extending its boundaries to central India.
 
• The annexation of Avanti was crucial as it eliminated a key rival and allowed Magadh to emerge as the most powerful kingdom in northern India during that era.
 
• This victory paved the way for later rulers of Magadh, such as the Nanda dynasty and Maurya dynasty, to further expand the empire and establish its supremacy.
